They were being accepted "in keeping with Liberia's long-standing tradition of being a country that has provided shelter to all those seeking refuge and protection from persecution, wars and other forms of conflict," the minister added, stressing it was a humanitarian arrangement. It is not clear if those coming to Liberia have protection orders. An initial group of 20 are due to land on Thursday and would be free to go when they wished or could apply for asylum, he said.
